title: ChaosBench: A Multi-Channel, Physics-Based Benchmark for Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Climate Prediction
venue: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
testbed_rationale: ChaosBench provides a fully standardized, multi-system (atmosphere, land, ocean, sea-ice), multi-decadal (45+ years) benchmark dataset specifically built for training and evaluating data-driven Earth system emulators and subseasonal forecasting models with clear scripts, HuggingFace dataset hosting, and operational NWP baselines.
pain_points: Predictive skill collapse on S2S horizons: state-of-the-art deterministic weather models collapse to or perform worse than unskilled climatology beyond 15-20 days.
Error propagation in autoregressive rollout leads to rapid loss of multi-scale structure and high spectral divergence (blurring/smoothing).
Extreme computational expense and data storage constraints for multi-decadal multi-channel global Earth system data across 124 variables.
S2S scale sensitivity to both initial conditions and boundary conditions (ocean, ice, land interactions).
extraction_notes: ChaosBench is directly developed under LEAP STC (Award #2019625). It establishes benchmark datasets across ERA5, ORAS5, and LRA5 alongside operational S2S forecast database outputs from WWRP/WCRP/ECMWF.
